model_type: Residual income on tangible book (bank): PV of dividends + PV of exit P/TBV x terminal TBVPS, discounted at cost of equity -- NOT a free-cash-flow DCF

valuation_philosophy.methodology: Residual-income / excess-return model on tangible book value, discounted at cost of equity (CoE). Implemented as PV(dividends per share, FY2027-FY2031) + PV(exit price-to-tangible-book multiple x FY2031 tangible book per share). With buybacks executed above tangible book the share count shrinks by less than the cash spent, which the per-share tangible book path captures explicitly.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_fcf_dcf: Westpac is an APRA-regulated deposit-taking bank. Reported operating cash flow swings with loan-book and deposit growth (FY2024 -19,767; FY2025 +9,489; H1 FY2026 -6,679, all AUD m) and is not a measure of owner earnings; customer deposits (745bn), debt issues (185bn) and loan capital (40bn) are funding raw material, not net debt. TotalDebt is deliberately NOT bridged, and no EBITDA, WACC-Gordon or SBC-to-FCF adjustment is used (SBC ~AUD 95m/yr is immaterial against 6.9bn NPAT and already expensed in ROTE).
valuation_philosophy.wacc_field_note: The 'wacc' field in every scenario is the COST OF EQUITY in AUD (the flows' own currency), not a blended WACC. Built as AUD 10-year government bond ~4.5% + equity risk premium ~5.0% x beta ~1.0 = 9.5% base; 9.0% bull, 10.5% bear (credit-cycle and NIM-compression premium).
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value_note: 'terminal_growth' per scenario carries the EXIT PRICE-TO-TANGIBLE-BOOK multiple applied to FY2031 tangible book per share (bear 1.2x, base 1.5x, bull 1.9x), in place of a Gordon perpetuity. Justified P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g): base terminal ROTE 12%, g 3%, CoE 9.5% -> 1.38x; 1.5x adds a modest oligopoly/franking premium. Bull 1.9x is roughly today's multiple (34.75/17.73 = 1.96x), i.e. the market keeps paying it. Sensitivity rows/columns vary CoE and exit P/TBV.

inputs.share_count_basis: Ordinary shares on issue less treasury shares (3,420.3m on issue at 31-Mar-2026; ~5m treasury), the basis Westpac uses for NTA per share and basic EPS. Diluted count (3,594m) assumes conversion of AT1 capital notes, which only occurs at a capital trigger and is excluded. Held flat except for modelled buybacks; SBC (~AUD 95m/yr) is satisfied by on-market purchases and is immaterial.
inputs.stub_note: 31-Mar-2026 NTA/share 17.73 rolled forward one half-year to the ~30-Sep-2026 valuation date: + H2 FY2026 earnings (11.3% annualised ROTE x 0.5 x 60.6bn = ~3.4bn) - 77c interim dividend paid 26-Jun-2026 (~2.6bn) = ~17.96/share. Other comprehensive income (reserves swung -2.7bn in H1 FY2026 on hedge/FX reserves) is not forecast.
inputs.balance_sheet_source: WBC.NZ_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (2026 Interim Financial Results): total equity attributable 70,761; intangible assets 10,204; NTA/share 17.73; CET1 12.42%
inputs.net_debt_note: Deposits (745,239), debt issues (185,491) and loan capital (40,218) are operating funding for a bank -- NOT net debt. Never bridged. The CSV TotalDebt column (225,709) is debt issues + loan capital and must not be used in an EV bridge.
inputs.fcf_note: FCF is not a valid concept for a bank; last_fcf deliberately null. reported_fcf shown only for audit (H1 FY2026 OCF -6,679 less capex 427).
inputs.sbc_source: WBC.NZ_Annual_FY2025.txt:6641 share-based payment arrangements 94 (FY2025 statement of changes in equity); FY2024 90
inputs.sbc_treatment: Immaterial (0.4% of revenue, 1.4% of NPAT) and already deducted in the ROTE that drives the model. No separate adjustment; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income IS the business (55,042 gross FY2025); not stripped.
inputs.buyback_status: AUD 3.5bn on-market buyback: 2.5bn completed by 31-Mar-2026 (88.8m shares at avg 28.01); only 50,000 shares (1.9m) bought in H1 FY2026 as the price rose to ~38; 1.0bn remains, extended to 10-Nov-2026. CET1 12.42% vs 11.25% target = ~2.7bn surplus after the interim dividend.
inputs.fy2026_guidance: Westpac gives no earnings guidance. Management framing at 1H26 (May-2026): CET1 above 11.25% target, ROTE improvement and cost-to-income reduction via UNITE as the performance measures; opex up 4% (2% ex RAMS sale costs); credit provisions raised for the Middle-East energy shock; mortgage growth 1.2x system, business lending +16%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows are AUD; WBC.NZ quotes NZD on the NZX. Per-share values computed in AUD then converted at AUDNZD 1.2435 (Yahoo AUDNZD=X, 2026-09-20T04:50Z). Parity check: WBC.AX 34.75 AUD (ASX close 2026-09-18) x 1.2435 = 43.21 NZD vs WBC.NZ 43.08 NZD -- within 0.3%, the NZX line trades at parity. Unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are NZD (quote currency); *_aud twins are the native basis.
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on tangible book at cost of equity (bank row of the dcf-methods routing table), same family as SRBK/SOFI/GEN.NZ. Fresh build 2026-09-20 -- no prior WBC.NZ DCF and no memory entry. Owner-FCF DCF rejected because OCF is a loan/deposit-flow artefact and deposits are not debt. Only three annual periods (FY2023-FY2025) plus two halves exist in the CSV, so CAGRs are 2-year. Price is the NZX regular close (not after-hours). Scenario drivers are this agent's judgement set 2026-09-20; the user has not yet reviewed them.

cost_of_equity.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows discounted at an AUD cost of equity: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.5% (Sep-2026, assumption -- verify against RBA/AOFM at next refresh) + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta ~1.0 = 9.5%. Big-4 Australian bank sell-side CoE range is 9-10%. Bear adds 1pp for a credit-cycle / NIM-compression regime; bull takes 0.5pp off for a benign rates and credit backdrop.

historical_growth.history_note: Only FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (plus H1 FY2025 and H1 FY2026) are in the CSV, so 3-year and 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed; 2-year CAGRs given. FCF CAGR is meaningless for a bank (OCF sign flips year to year).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: sustainable_growth = ROTE x (1 - payout) = 11.5% x 25% ~ 2.9% (tangible-book compounding rate); revenue/EPS/equity have been flat since FY2023
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 2-yr CAGR 0.2% vs revenue 1.7% and EPS -0.8%: all inside a +/-2pp band; no material divergence, the business is ex-growth at the top line and value comes from the ~11% ROTE paid out at ~75%.

bear.rationale: NIM compresses toward 1.8% as mortgage competition and deposit mix shift persist, credit costs step up to ~20bps through the energy-price shock, UNITE delivers cost-out late; ROTE slides to 9.5%, at or below CoE. Payout trimmed to 72%, no further buybacks (capital retained for RWA growth and the higher provisioning). Exit at 1.2x TBV, the low end of Westpac's 2015-2024 range, at a 10.5% CoE.

base.rationale: ROTE grinds from 11.2% to 12.0% as UNITE lowers cost-to-income from ~53% toward 50%, NIM holds ~1.9%, credit costs normalise ~10-12bps. 75% payout (FY2025 73%, 1H26 77%); the remaining 1.0bn of the buyback completes in FY2027 at ~1.96x TBV, then retention funds ~5% RWA growth with no further buybacks. Exit 1.5x TBV vs justified 1.38x; CoE 9.5%.

bull.rationale: Rates and credit stay benign, UNITE hits its cost targets early, ROTE reaches 13.5% (peer-leading ex-CBA). Surplus capital above 11.25% CET1 recycled through 1.0-1.5bn/yr buybacks at today's multiple. Exit at 1.9x TBV (today's multiple sustained) at a 9.0% CoE.

bear.fcf_note: Not free cash flow. A bank's OCF is meaningless; these are projected fully-franked dividends per share in AUD.

base.fcf_note: Not free cash flow. A bank's OCF is meaningless; these are projected fully-franked dividends per share in AUD.

bull.fcf_note: Not free cash flow. A bank's OCF is meaningless; these are projected fully-franked dividends per share in AUD.

bear.implied_exit_multiple_note: Exit price-to-tangible-book multiple (explicit judgement), not an EV/FCF multiple.

base.implied_exit_multiple_note: Exit price-to-tangible-book multiple (explicit judgement), not an EV/FCF multiple.

bull.implied_exit_multiple_note: Exit price-to-tangible-book multiple (explicit judgement), not an EV/FCF multiple.

entry_price.methodology: Entry = PV(scenario DPS FY2027-FY2031 at 15%) + PV(scenario exit P/TBV x FY2031 TBVPS at 15%). The exit multiple is an explicit judgement (not a rate-derived Gordon value), so it is kept and only the discounting uses the hurdle -- the same treatment as RYM.NZ/GEN.NZ exit-multiple models. Computed in AUD, converted at the FX rate above.

required_return_table.note: NZD values (quote currency); each row rebuilds PV of dividends and the exit value at that rate. The 9.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = cost of equity (%), columns = exit price-to-tangible-book multiple on FY2031 TBVPS; base-case ROTE/payout/buyback path. Values in NZD (matrix) and AUD (matrix_aud).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear is lifted to 25% because the H1 FY2026 provision top-up for the Middle-East energy shock, the NIM drift to 1.89% and UNITE execution risk are live, and the stock already prices the bull case (1.96x TBV, ~17x TTM EPS); bull is cut to 25% because the bull case requires the market to keep paying today's multiple AND ROTE to reach 13.5%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases coincide (SBC immaterial and already inside ROTE); band collapsed, band_position null.

justified_ptbv_check.note: Market P/TBV 1.96x exceeds even the bull-case justified multiple; the price embeds either a sub-8% CoE or ROTE >15%, neither of which Westpac has delivered in a decade.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
